full_judgment: 9. Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that according to second   proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended by the amending Act XXIV of 1997 which came into force on 19.11.1997 the appellant was required to wait for a decision on his departmental appeal for two months i.e. upto 24.03.2000 and he was required to come to the Administrative Tribunals for relief against his dismissal within 6 months. He then submits that the appellant was required to file application before the Administrative Tribunal within 24.09.2000 according t. second proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended but he filed the application before the Administrative Tribunal on 23.11.2000 i.e. long after the expiry of the period of limitation. He submits that although according to the last proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended the application before the Administrative Tribunal would have been within time but limitation provided for in the last proviso to Section 4(2) of the said Act is not available to the applicant because the period of limitation in the second proviso to the aforesaid section is the governing provision compared to the last proviso to the said section as per interpolation of the statuary period. He finally submits that the application filed by the appellant before the Administrative Tribunal was hopelessly barred by limitation and the Member of the Administrative Tribunal and the Administrative Appellant Tribunal rightly decided the limitation question against the appellant and as such the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
